findings.text: Insertion rebalancing is exposed through two entry points sharing one internal insertion engine. The plain variant always supplies a no-operation rotation notifier for trees without augmentation, while the augmented variant forwards a caller supplied rotation notifier so derived subtree data can be maintained during restructuring.

Removal rebalancing is available as a standalone color repair routine plus higher level erase helpers. One helper removes a plain node and then invokes color repair only when the low level removal reports further work, while the linked variant first unlinks intrusive list neighbours and the cached leftmost pointer before delegating to plain removal and clearing the link marker.

Ordered navigation offers successor and predecessor plus postorder iteration. Successor and predecessor return the adjacent key in sorted order or absence at the ends and for detached markers, while postorder offers the deepest leftmost start point and a step that visits children before parents.

Node substitution swaps a victim with a replacement that inherits links and color, repointing children and parent. A second variant provides identical logical effect but orders the final parent link after a read copy update barrier so concurrent readers observe valid downstream references.

Deletion repair proceeds as a loop that restores equal dark height on the deficient side. A red sibling triggers a parent rotation that normalizes the sibling to black. With a black sibling whose descendants are both black or missing, the sibling is reddened and the deficiency either resolves at a red parent or propagates upward. An inner red descendant triggers a sibling side rotation that converts the shape to the outer case, which then performs a parent rotation with recoloring of the involved trio and terminates. The mirror side follows the same progression with left and right exchanged, and every structural rotation notifies augmentation.

During deletion repair the deficient position is always black or empty on entry, never the overall root, and every leaf path through the deficient side is short by exactly one black relative to other paths until the loop resolves or ascends.

A valid tree keeps keys in nondecreasing sorted order under inorder walk, forbids a red node from having a red parent or from occupying the root, keeps the number of black nodes identical across all root to leaf paths that end in a partially filled position, and maintains enough nodes to satisfy the logarithmic height bound implied by that black count.

When augmentation is enabled each node stores the maximum of its own value and the augmented maxima of existing children, and insertion along the search path eagerly raises ancestors that are smaller than the new value before linking.
The test harness element pairs an opaque key with an intrusive tree link and, for augmentation trials, a base value plus a cached subtree aggregate.
A reference record contains a list anchor usable in either the active set or a quarantine set, a liveness flag, and two stack depot handles capturing allocation and release origins.
Directory statistics keep a lifetime total and a live count plus a trailing flexible array where each slot pairs an allocation stack identity with the number of live records sharing it.

Marking a directory dead for filesystem reclamation acquires the directory index lock in interrupt safe mode separately for the entry index and the link index, sets a dead marker for the directory key in each, releases each lock, then queues background reclamation work.

A loadable test module allocates a configurable array of trial nodes, seeds deterministic randomness, exercises plain and cached plus plain and augmented insertion removal traversal and validation, frees the array, fails initialization when allocation fails, and otherwise fails loading after the trials so the module unloads immediately; unload only emits a notice.

Reference counting exposes slow paths for acquisition and release that resolve boundary conditions outside the inline fast path and report whether acquisition succeeded and whether the releaser may retire the object.

Acquisition in the slow path fails and parks the counter in the middle of the dead zone when the observed value already indicates release, otherwise succeeds; if the observed value exceeds the allowed maximum it emits a one time saturation warning and parks the counter at the saturated marker to avoid wrap while leaking the object.

Release in the slow path attempts to transition from empty to dead with release ordering and acquire follow through, succeeding only when no concurrent acquisition intervened; an already dead observation triggers a one time imbalance warning and reparks at dead, while a saturated observation restores the saturated marker, both without granting retirement permission.

Exceeding the maximum count intentionally leaks memory rather than allowing counter wrap, and releasing more often than acquiring is treated as a programming error that warns and stabilizes the counter instead of permitting teardown.

Tree links are published with ordered writes so readers observe consistent child pointers, and only the read copy update replacement variant is safe for concurrent traversal because it delays the parent link update until downstream references are visible; other restructuring assumes external exclusion.

Traversal guards against detached markers by returning absence without dereferencing further, and postorder start returns absence for an empty root while postorder step returns absence for missing input, so callers must treat null as end of sequence rather than error.

Reference tracking fixes the captured stack depth at 16 [CITED lib/ref_tracker.c::REF_TRACKER_STACK_ENTRIES] entries and the diagnostic formatting buffer at 1024 [CITED lib/ref_tracker.c::STACK_BUF_SIZE] bytes.

A dead tracking directory is denoted by aliasing the first attribute mark, diagnostics carry a fixed prefix naming the subsystem followed by colon space, and trial trees begin from the standard empty cached root initializer.

Trial insertion descends by key comparison to a vacant link, links the new element, then triggers color repair, tracking whether the descent ever went right to inform the cached leftmost hint; removal delegates to plain or cached erase and augmented removal forwards the maximum callback set.
Validation confirms that both direct postorder iteration and the safe container iteration visit exactly the expected number of elements, complementing inorder ordering and color checks.
A helper macro declares a static tunable with an initial value and exposes it as a read only module parameter with descriptive text.
